title: Power Apps: display density settings for model-driven apps
summary: Hold: Microsoft does not substantiate the assurances that no new permission is needed or that no budget control applies. The instruction to find the setting's unique name in the Add existing setting definition dialog is also unverified. The roadmap details and the documented density behaviour are supported.

claims.quote: If you process large volumes of data, such as in high-velocity data-entry, field service, or manufacturing scenarios, choose a denser display to see more information on screen at once.

claims.claim: Microsoft's feature documentation describes no new data access, storage or sharing mechanism for display density.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" force user preference admin security storage budget cap. Opened appearance-settings, modern-fluent-design and fluent-modern-theming; no new business-data access, storage or sharing mechanism is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The setting needs no new permission and touches no permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" permissions role Power Apps; Power Apps "display density" license licensing pricing meter permissions roles. Opened appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings; neither states that no new permission is needed.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change documented: the setting needs no new permission' with 'The appearance page does not specify the permissions needed to change display density.' Remove 'or permissions' from the risk rationale's 'touches no data or permissions'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The appearance page does not specify security roles for editing environment or app density values.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" permissions role Power Apps. Opened appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings; appearance-settings names admins and makers but specifies no security role for density.

claims.claim: The general settings page describes an environment administrator adding an environment value and an application author adding an app value.
claims.quote:
an environment administrator in a customer's organization can add a setting environment value
an application author in the same environment above, can add a setting app value

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specifically for the display-density change has not been published, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" license licensing pricing meter permissions roles; Power Apps model driven apps licensing requirements Power Apps Premium Dynamics 365. Opened appearance-settings, pricing-billing-skus and powerapps-licensing-faq; no density-specific licence rule.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The appearance page and roadmap name no density licence or meter; the appearance page's only stated prerequisite is wave 2.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" license licensing pricing meter permissions roles. Read the roadmap record and full appearance-settings page: neither names a licence or meter; the appearance note requires the header and navigation refresh (wave 2).

claims.claim: No meter specifically for display density is documented at the time of writing, November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" license licensing pricing meter permissions roles. Opened appearance-settings, pricing-billing-skus and powerapps-licensing-faq; read pay-as-you-go-meters search excerpts. No density-specific meter found; general Power Apps meters exist.

claims.claim: No cap or budget control applies because no density meter is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" force user preference admin security storage budget cap; Power Apps "display density" license licensing pricing meter permissions roles. Opened appearance-settings and pricing-billing-skus; no passage says no cap or budget control applies.
claims.fix: Delete ', so no cap or budget control applies'. Keep the narrower sentence: 'No meter is documented for this feature at the time of writing (November 2026).' Undocumented feature-specific billing does not establish that budget controls are inapplicable.

claims.claim: An existing setting can be added in Power Apps through Solutions > solution > Add existing > More > Setting.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Solutions.
From the list of solutions, open the solution you want to add the setting to.
In the command bar, select Add existing > More > Setting.
claims.fix: Add to the environment row's note: 'The settings guide requires Solution preview on in the Solutions command bar for these steps.' The cited guide explicitly qualifies its solution instructions this way.

claims.claim: SaveSettingValue accepts SettingName and Value and supports an organisation-level override without an AppUniqueName.
claims.quote:
Creates or updates app/organization level override.
AppUniqueName | Edm.String | True | False | Model-driven app unique name (Optional).
SettingName | Edm.String | False | False | Setting definition unique name (Required).
Value | Edm.String | False | False
claims.fix: Replace the prose description in api.call with 'POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue; JSON body: {"SettingName":"<setting definition unique name>","Value":"<value>"}'. Retain the warning that the density setting's unique name must be established before use. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/use-web-api-actions in sources for POST and the versioned unbound-action request format; the existing reference supplies the action and parameters.

claims.quote: In the app designer select Settings on the command bar.

claims.claim: SaveSettingValue accepts AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value for an app-level override.
claims.quote:
Creates or updates app/organization level override.
AppUniqueName | Edm.String | True | False | Model-driven app unique name (Optional).
SettingName | Edm.String | False | False | Setting definition unique name (Required).
Value | Edm.String | False | False
claims.fix: Replace api.call with 'POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue; JSON body: {"AppUniqueName":"<app unique name>","SettingName":"<setting definition unique name>","Value":"<value>"}'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/use-web-api-actions in sources for the POST request format. claims.claim: App-setting changes must be saved and published to take effect.
claims.quote:
You must select Publish to activate an app settings change.
Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: The general settings mechanism uses a definition default, an optional environment value and an optional app value, in increasing precedence.
claims.quote:
A setting environment value can be used to override the default value, as specified in the setting definition.
A setting app value can be used to override the default value, as specified in the setting definition, and the setting environment value (if one exists).

claims.claim: The appearance page names no density-specific API, and the generic SaveSettingValue reference does not name this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" "SaveSettingValue" SettingName enforce permissions; "SaveSettingValue" "POST". Opened appearance-settings, savesettingvalue and get-update-setting-value-using-code. The feature page names no API; the generic reference names no density setting.

claims.claim: The cited documentation does not supply the unique name of the Display density setting definition.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" "unique name" Power Apps; Power Apps "display density" "SaveSettingValue" SettingName enforce permissions. Opened appearance-settings, create-edit-configure-settings, app-properties and savesettingvalue; no density setting-definition unique name supplied.

claims.claim: The Add existing setting definition dialog lets the reader confirm the setting's unique name before scripting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" "unique name" Power Apps. Opened create-edit-configure-settings and appearance-settings. The former documents selecting settings in Add existing setting definition, but does not state that this dialog exposes their unique names.
claims.fix: Remove ', so confirm it in the Add existing setting definition dialog before scripting'. End the sentence at 'the setting's unique name is not given on the pages read'. This retains the verified prerequisite without inventing where its value can be obtained.

claims.claim: Learn does not document forcing a specific density over an explicit personal selection, apart from disabling density.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps "display density" force user preference admin security storage budget cap. Opened appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings: personal choices override defaults; Off suppresses density. No other density enforcement found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to take stock of appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Ask makers which model-driven apps already have the header and navigation refresh enabled'. The table contains only environment display-density defaults and app display-density defaults/Off.
claims.fix: The first Before rollout checklist step takes stock of the header and navigation refresh, which has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the verified prerequisite and its app-designer path under Scope. Do not add a control row.
